articles.title: Tempestade no DF: Defesa Civil e Inmet emitem alerta para quarta | G1
articles.standfirst: Alerta de tempestade começa à 0h desta quarta-feira (23) e segue até quinta (24). Inmet prevê chuva de até 50 mm por dia, ventos de até 60 km/h e possibilidade de granizo.
articles.summary: Tempestade no DF pode atingir 50 mm de chuva com ventos de 60 km/h e queda de granizo nesta quarta-feira, conforme alertas da Defesa Civil e do Inmet.
articles.body:
ARQUIVO: Fotógrafo do DF registra tempestade de raios sobre Taguatinga e Samambaia. — Foto: Léo Caldas/Divulgação

A Defesa Civil emitiu, nesta terça-feira (22), um alerta de tempestade para todo o Distrito Federal válido para os próximos dias. ⛈️

O órgão orienta a população a procurar um local seguro em caso de ventos fortes e evitar pontos de alagamento durante a chuva.

O alerta foi enviado por celular aos moradores do DF. Em caso de risco, a orientação é ligar para a Defesa Civil, pelo telefone 199.

Segundo aviso do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia ( Inmet ), o alerta é de perigo potencia l – o primeiro nível de severidade – e é válido a partir da 0h desta quarta-feira (23) até 23h59 de quinta-feira (24).

A previsão é de chuva entre 20 e 30 milímetros por hora ou até 50 mm ao longo do dia, além de ventos de 40 km/h a 60 km/h e possibilidade de queda de granizo.

Antes da tempestade, o Distrito Federal ainda enfrenta um alerta de baixa umidade, válido até as 23h59 desta terça-feira (22). Ao longo do dia, a umidade relativa do ar chegou a ficar entre 30% e 20%.

De acordo com Olívio Bahia, meteorologista do Inmet, os dois avisos podem ocorrer na sequência e até mesmo no mesmo dia.

"Podemos ter baixa umidade e, depois, com o calor e o aumento do conteúdo de água na atmosfera, ter chuvas e temporais também. Está muito quente. O calor somado a umidade (conteúdo de vapor d'água ao longo da atmosfera) tem como resultado a instabilidade", explicou Olívio Bahia.

Ou seja: o DF pode sair de um cenário de baixa umidade nesta terça para chuva e temporais a partir da madrugada de quarta. 🌧️

O Inmet aponta baixo risco de corte de energia elétrica, estragos em plantações, queda de galhos de árvores e alagamentos.

Durante as rajadas de vento, a recomendação é não se abrigar debaixo de árvores e não estacionar veículos próximos a torres de transmissão e placas de propaganda.

O instituto também orienta a população a evitar aparelhos eletrônicos ligados à tomada durante a tempestade.

Em situações de emergência, além da Defesa Civil (199), o Corpo de Bombeiros pode ser acionado pelo telefone 193.

articles.title: Como Rick foi convencido a gravar 'Filha', um dos seus maiores sucessos e destaque em festas de debutantes | G1
articles.standfirst: Gravada inicialmente em tiragem íntima para convidados, faixa virou um dos maiores sucessos da trajetória da dupla Rick e Renner.
articles.summary: Gravada inicialmente em tiragem íntima para convidados, faixa virou um dos maiores sucessos da trajetória da dupla Rick e Renner.
articles.body:
Um dos maiores sucessos da dupla Rick e Renner era a canção "Filha". Composta por Rick, a canção que fala do amor de um pai pela filha acabou virando uma espécie de hino para festas de debutantes.

A música foi composta em homenagem ao aniversário de 15 anos de Mônica Nascimento, filha do cantor.

"Cheguei pra ela e falei: 'Filha, o que você quer de presente? Pode escolher o que quiser'. Ela me surpreendeu e falou que queria fazer uma festa."

"Eu queria eternizar esse momento. Peguei o violão e escrevi a música 'Filha'. Fui no estúdio, gravei, mas não contei pra ninguém. Fiz um disco com 500 cópias pros convidados e entreguei ali na festa. Demos essa música pra algumas pessoas."

Entre essas pessoas estavam, além de radialistas, a própria filha e seu parceiro de música, Renner. Todos gostaram bastante da versão e queriam que eles gravassem a faixa no próximo disco da dupla.

"Eu não queria, mas ele [Renner] queria colocar no disco. Eu falava que essa música era pessoal, não queria gravar. No final, a gente colocou a música no disco e se tornou a música da família", comentou Rick.

A música acabou sendo gravada em 2001 no álbum "É Dez, É Cem, É Mil" e virou um dos maiores sucessos da dupla, presente em diversas festas de debutantes pelo Brasil.

Dois dias antes de o helicóptero em que estava cair em Santa Catarina, o cantor Rick participou de uma homenagem surpresa preparada por um pai para a filha durante uma festa de 15 anos em Sorriso (MT), no último sábado (19).

Nas imagens publicadas nas redes sociais, a aniversariante Maria Bergamin aparece ao lado do pai, Willian Bergamin, durante a comemoração. A surpresa acontece quando Rick e Renner entram na festa cantando "Filha".

Geraldo Antônio de Carvalho , o Rick, nasceu no Tocantins em 5 de dezembro de 1966. Ele se mudou com a família para Brasília aos seis anos e começou a cantar em bares aos nove, ao lado de uma das irmãs, chegando a ter problemas com o Juizado de Menores por sua pouca idade. Ele faria 60 anos em dezembro.

A dupla Rick e Renner foi formada nos anos 1980, em Brasília, e começou a fazer sucesso nos anos 1990, antes da explosão do chamado sertanejo universitário, que renovou o estilo. Entre os principais sucessos da dupla estão "Ela é demais" (do refrão "uma deusa, uma louca, uma feiticeira") e "Nos bares da cidade".

Rick, cantor da dupla Rick e Renner — Foto: Divulgação

A dupla Rick e Renner foi formada em meados dos anos 1980. O parceiro de Rick era Ivair Reis Gonçalves , o Renner, nascido em Brasília em 19 de novembro de 1971.

Renner começou a cantar rock aos 14 anos. Aos 16, tornou-se pai e passou a ajudar a sustentar a família com o dinheiro que ganhava com a música.

Rick e Renner começaram a carreira se apresentando em bares e chegaram a gravar um LP independente. A dupla recebeu ajuda de Zezé Di Camargo e Luciano, que os apresentaram ao produtor Manoel Nenzinho Pinto.

A parceria abriu caminho para a gravação do primeiro disco pela gravadora Continental. Entre os destaques do álbum estavam músicas como "Preciso te Encontrar", "Você Decide", "Olhando nos Teus Olhos", "Mal de Amor" e "A Gente Sempre se Entende".

Depois do primeiro trabalho, os dois se mudaram para São Paulo para dar continuidade à carreira artística.

O cantor Rick Sollo — Foto: Reprodução/ EPTV

A trajetória de Rick e Renner ganhou força ao longo dos anos 1990, com sucessivos lançamentos que consolidaram a dupla no sertanejo romântico.

O grande salto veio em 1998, com o álbum Mil Vezes Cantarei, que trouxe “Ela é Demais” , principal sucesso da carreira da dupla. A música permaneceu por cinco meses consecutivos nas paradas de sucesso e se tornou um dos maiores símbolos da trajetória dos cantores.

Até hoje ela é a música mais tocada da dupla nas plataformas de streaming.

No ano seguinte, o álbum Instante Mágico ampliou ainda mais a popularidade de Rick e Renner, com sucessos como “Muleca”, “Cara-de-Pau”, “Fim de Semana” e “Na Pontinha do Pé”, esta última com participação do grupo Molejo.

Nos anos seguintes, Rick e Renner mantiveram uma sequência de lançamentos e apresentações pelo país. Em 2003, para celebrar uma década de carreira, a dupla lançou um álbum acústico que reuniu alguns de seus principais sucessos, entre eles “Ela é Demais”, “O Amor e Eu” e “Paixão de Peão”. No mesmo ano, os cantores também lançaram o primeiro DVD da carreira.

Até 2007, Rick e Renner já haviam vendido mais de 7 milhões de discos e realizavam, em média, 150 shows por ano. A sequência de trabalhos manteve a dupla entre os nomes de destaque do sertanejo brasileiro, enquanto “Ela é Demais” permanecia como um dos principais sucessos e marcas da carreira dos dois.

Já no fim de 2010, Rick e Renner anunciaram o interrompimento do trabalho da dupla, após uma trajetória de 25 anos. Naquele momento, os dois haviam lançado 16 CDs e dois DVDs.

Na época, Rick disse em entrevista ao g1 sobre a decisão de seguir em carreira solo, com nome artístico Rick Sollo: "Estou muito consciente do que quero no momento. Tenho pedido no Twitter que os fãs compreendam a decisão. Eu não tenho problemas com ela. Estou neste exato momento começando a ensaiar um show novo."

Renner seguiu carreira solo na música gospel, com ajuda de Rick.

"Se eu tivesse que ficar em dupla, ficaria com o Renner. Cada um vai seguir um caminho. Nada impede que nos juntemos novamente, façamos uma turnê. Estamos só dando um tempo. Como não teve brigas, tem chance de retorno", ele também afirmou em 2010.

Rick lançou os álbuns solo "Pronto pra te amar", de 2011, e "Foi Deus..." de 2015, sem o mesmo destaque dos sucessos da dupla.

Após 8 anos separados, a dupla voltou a trabalhar junta em 2018. Na retomada, lançou o CD "Seguir em Frente", pela Radar Records, e iniciou uma turnê com o mesmo nome.

O álbum reuniu composições de Rick, incluindo "Eu Mereço", "Filha", "Esse Amor é Você", "Nos Bares da Cidade" e "Como Assim".

Em 2020, durante o período de isolamento social provocado pela pandemia de coronavírus, Rick e Renner fizeram apresentações ao vivo pela internet.

Entre elas estavam as lives "Em prol do Estado do Maranhão", que arrecadou dinheiro e cestas básicas por meio de doações, e "At Home". Juntas, as transmissões ultrapassaram 4 milhões de acessos.

A dupla lançou alguns singles nas plataformas de streaming nos últimos anos, como "Estou aqui!", de 2024, "Porque o Bruto Chora", de 2025 e "O Caçador", de 2026, o mais recente.

A dupla estava rodando o Brasil com a turnê comemorativa "Em nome da música".

articles.title: India teams up with EU, Canada & others to defend multilateralism; EAM says rules must be scrupulously followed
articles.summary: India News: India joined the EU, Canada, Australia and several other countries in co-sponsoring a declaration expressing a joint commitment to multilateralism, in.
articles.body: India joined the EU, Canada, Australia and several other countries in co-sponsoring a declaration expressing a joint commitment to multilateralism, international law, peace and prosperity, while expressing concern over escalating conflicts, trade disruption, power politics protectionism and coercion.The declaration followed the announcement of a new initiative titled Partners for Multilateralism (P4M) on the margins of the UN General Assembly that aims to make multilateral bodies more “representative, effective, legitimate and trusted” through middle-power cooperation, amid growing fragmentation and violations of international law.Drawing attention to geopolitical tensions, conflicts and extreme competition, foreign minister S Jaishankar said multilateralism will be best served when international law, rules, and norms are scrupulously observed.Other declaration co-sponsors included Brazil, Barbados and Kenya, making P4M a diverse group of countries that bridges – unlike the G7 and BRICS - the gap between the West and Global South. After the co-sponsors, 16 other countries signed off on the declaration that flagged increasing use of economic interdependence as a source of leverage, disrupting trade, supply chains, investment and development finance in messages directed at both US and China.The declaration stressed reform of multilateral institutions, including the UN, to promote fair trade, prevent conflicts and protect rule of law, while backing fair, open, resilient, predictable and inclusive economic cooperation, including more diversified and resilient global supply chains.The declaration said that the multilateral system founded on the UN Charter remained indispensable, as it had helped provide a framework for peace, decolonisation, prosperity, and human dignity. However, the declaration also said that it must now respond to a world that is more interconnected and complex, more contested and more multipolar.“We affirm the need to uphold and enforce the rules, principles and commitments that remain essential to international order, while renewing and reforming the multilateral system so that it is more effective, representative, inclusive and fit for purpose,” said the declaration, while stressing the joint commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, peaceful settlement of disputes and prohibition of the threat or use of force.The inaugural meeting was co-hosted by European Council President Antonio Costa who said that the P4M will serve as a global network for dialogue, coalition-building and practical cooperation, helping us coordinate our response to shared challenges, with the UN at its core.As he underlined the need for multilateralism to assert itself strongly in these times, Jaishankar also pointed to the issue of terrorism. “The future of peace and international security, of climate action and climate justice, of emerging technologies and development finance ,of countering terrorism and strengthening supply chain, and of ensuring disaster resilience and preparing for pandemics, all depend on a will to cooperate,” he said.The minister also flagged the 4F crises of fuel, food, fertilizer and finance cannot be left to itself, saying where new capabilities and concerns arise, there is a very powerful case for frameworks and guardrails.“Where there is a threat of chokepoints dominance and disruption, de-risking and diversifying must be encouraged. And where there is a compelling cause or a powerful case, the like-minded must have the confidence to come together,” said Jaishankar, stressing the need for reformed multilateralism.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: How rising house prices have forced Taiwan to settle for ‘haunted homes’
articles.summary: News News: Property prices in Taiwan have seen a significant rise, forcing a growing number of buyers to turn towards homes with troubled pasts to find an afford.
articles.body: Property prices in Taiwan have seen a significant rise, forcing a growing number of buyers to turn towards homes with troubled pasts to find an affordable way to live. “Haunted houses” or “murder homes,” also known in Mandarin as Xiong Zhai, these properties are where a previous occupant died in violent or otherwise disturbing circumstances.The Times reported that the more violent the death, the lower the asking price tends to be, with some properties selling for as little as half the market rate.The trend comes as Taiwan's economy continues to grow, expanding by 14 per cent in the first half of 2026, driven by the island's AI and semiconductor industries. However, the economic boom has not made housing affordable for everyone, pushing some buyers towards properties that carry a social stigma.But the discounts come with difficulties. Banks are often reluctant to lend against such properties because they may struggle to recover their money if a borrower defaults, given the difficulty of reselling them.“People might see the property as inauspicious and believe it could affect their luck,” real estate agent Wu Kaiwen, told the Times, explaining the reluctance to finance such homes.The hesitation reflects Taiwan's continuing spiritual traditions despite its status as a technology hub.During “ghost month”, which runs until mid-September, people believe the gates of the underworld open and spirits return to earth. Some temples leave out food offerings during the period to appease them.Many buyers who choose a xiong zhai arrange ceremonies intended to release any lingering spirits from the property before moving in.Spiritual practitioners say such ceremonies are performed with the aim of helping a lingering spirit leave and cleansing the property so that negative energy associated with the death does not affect the new occupants.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Meet Halima Kedir: Ethiopian woman mocked for planting trees, but her green garden inspired neighbours to follow her example
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Halima Kedir, 35, from the Berbere district of Ethiopia's Oromia region, was mocked and discouraged by her neighbours when she first began planting tr.
articles.body: Halima Kedir, 35, from the Berbere district of Ethiopia's Oromia region, was mocked and discouraged by her neighbours when she first began planting trees. Years later, her garden is lush with banana, olive and grevillea trees, and the same neighbours who doubted her are now following her lead. Her story sits within the UN's wider Green Legacy Initiative, a national tree-planting drive aiming for 50 billion trees by 2030. Here's how one woman's persistence helped shift attitudes in her community, and where Ethiopia's broader reforestation effort stands today.How Halima Kedir's tree planting was first met with mockery in BerbereWhen Kedir first began planting trees, she told The Guardian her neighbours discouraged her outright. "They thought I was striving for nothing, but with time, many are realising that trees can be part of the solution to our problems as a way to fight climate change and food insecurity," she said. Kedir has lost count of how many trees she has planted, becoming an accidental environmentalist in the process. Despite severe water shortages in her area, she has had to walk for about an hour to fetch water to keep her seedlings alive.Kedir's persistence changed her neighbours' mindsAs Kedir's trees took root and her surroundings grew greener, attitudes in the community began to shift. She has said that everything has changed since those early days, with the very people who once tried to dissuade her now said to be envious of her effort and commitment. Her neighbour, Fate Abdulahi, was later drawn into tree planting after seeing what Kedir had achieved, saying she proved the doubters wrong and has become a role model, someone willing to find local solutions to community issues. Kedir's bond with her trees has also been described in maternal terms, rooted in the Oromo tradition of guddifachaa, the practice of adopting a child into the community; a connection captured in her own words, that just as children are adopted in that tradition, her trees are seen much the same way, like her own.Ethiopia's Green Legacy Initiative and the scale of national tree plantingKedir's efforts form part of a much larger national picture. According to The Guardian, between 2000 and 2025, Ethiopia lost 560,000 hectares of tree cover to agricultural expansion, commercial logging and charcoal use. In response, the government launched the Green Legacy Initiative in 2019, and the deforestation rate has since slowed, falling from 92,000 hectares annually in 2013 to 27,703 hectares in 2023, while forest cover rose from 15.5% to 23.6% over the same period. The government says it has planted 48 billion trees in seven years, including a reported 353 million seedlings in a single day, with a target of 50 billion by 2030.Questions over seedling survival rates and what comes nextLong-term success depends on how many planted trees actually survive, and reliable data remains scarce. A government-backed committee reported average seedling survival rates of 83.4% in 2019 and 79% in 2020, though these figures have drawn scepticism; separate research found nearly half of reforestation trees in parts of Asia failed to survive beyond five years, and 10 of 15 Ethiopian tree-planting schemes examined by researchers fell short of 50% success. Yitebitu Moges of the UN Environment Programme in Ethiopia told The Guardian the highlands have seen the greatest success and that a systematic survival study is now under way, adding that even partial survival still delivers gains in moisture retention, soil health and carbon sequestration. articles.title: Peacemaker with a warning to annihilate: The major contradictions in Trump's UN speech
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump returned to the United Nations podium Tuesday wearing two very different hats. One moment he was the global peacemaker who h.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump returned to the United Nations podium Tuesday wearing two very different hats. One moment he was the global peacemaker who had "ended eight wars", the next he was threatening to wipe out Iran.The gap between these two versions captures the uncertain order Trump has built, or perhaps enabled, during his second term in the White House.Trump used much of his address to the General Debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly to list his achievements, much as he did a year ago when he cast himself as the standout contender for the Nobel Peace Prize. This year, though, the prize went unmentioned. Instead, his tone hardened, with attacks on the International Criminal Court (ICC), the UN's climate agenda and Unesco.Trump also pointed to his effort to launch a "Board of Peace" in January, which appeared another swipe at the UN, with him at one point suggesting his new creation might end up replacing it.Ironically, within a month of the board's creation, the US and Israel launched a joint military operation against Iran, one that has continued in some form since."Since I took office, it has been my great honour to settle eight wars, and in so doing, become friendly with the leaders of many of those countries. It was a great honour to do it. Numerous of these wars have gone on for many years and even decades," he told the assembled leaders.He credited his success to what he called "very special relationships", along with the use and threat of tariffs.Among the conflicts he claimed to have resolved were the disputes between Cambodia and Thailand, Kosovo and Serbia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, Pakistan and India, and Armenia and Azerbaijan, as well as the war in Gaza.He repeated a claim India has long rejected, that he brokered peace between India and Pakistan last year."The Prime Minister of Pakistan, terrific man, said that Donald Trump was responsible for saving 30 million lives and probably many more than that," Trump said.India has always maintained the ceasefire came from direct talks between the two countries' military operations chiefs, with Pakistani DGMO seeking the truce amid Operation Sindoor.He also mentioned Russia and Ukraine, saying his team is "working very closely" with both sides. "We will get that one done. It's going to happen, I think, more quickly than people understand," he said.Peacemaker to annihilatorHaving spent much of the speech basking in the image of a dealmaker, Trump turned to Iran, warning that Tehran must either negotiate with Washington or face destruction.Iran would never be allowed to have nuclear weapons, he said, adding that he faces "a big decision to make.""Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world? Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?"He went further still, asking, "Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?" He then predicted a deal was more likely once the midterm elections were over, since Iran was "waiting to see how I do in the midterm election," despite Trump not being on the ballot himself.Lo and behold, Trump's speech offered a portrait of a President who saw no contradiction in claiming the mantle of peacemaker while reserving the language of annihilation for those who resist his terms.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A volunteer sorting old Royal Navy papers found a rare 1776 US Declaration of Independence copy; it is one of 11 surviving Exeter printings and the only one outside the US
articles.summary: US News: A volunteer sorting old Royal Navy papers at The National Archives in London has uncovered a rare 1776 printing of the US Declaration of Independence,.
articles.body: A volunteer sorting old Royal Navy papers at The National Archives in London has uncovered a rare 1776 printing of the US Declaration of Independence, found among letters sent by a British captain after capturing an American privateer ship. The document is one of only 11 surviving copies printed in Exeter, New Hampshire, and is now the only known example outside the United States. Discovered in May 2026 by volunteer Michael Scurr while cataloguing Admiralty correspondence, the fragile broadside had travelled across the Atlantic as wartime evidence before resting quietly in a box of 18th-century naval letters for more than two centuries, according to The National Archives.A chance find in a box of captains’ lettersThe discovery came as part of the America 250 project, which is cataloguing Royal Navy admirals’ and captains’ letters from the American Revolutionary War to coincide with the 250th anniversary of US independence. Michael Scurr, a volunteer on the project, was working through a box of correspondence from Captain Thomas Fitzherbert of HMS Raisonable when he noticed a reference to documents seized from a captured American vessel. One item, described simply as “another paper,” turned out to be the Exeter printing of the Declaration.For Scurr, the moment was both thrilling and humbling. Handling a document that had helped announce the birth of a new nation, in the same year that the United States is marking its 250th anniversary, underlined how much history can still be hidden in plain sight within vast archival collections. His find shows how volunteers, working steadily through uncatalogued or under-examined records, can change what we know about major historical events.The Exeter Declarations and why they are rareThe Declaration of Independence was first adopted by the Continental Congress in Philadelphia on 4 July 1776. In the days that followed, printers across the Thirteen Colonies rushed to produce their own editions, spreading the news of independence as widely as possible. One of these printers was Robert Luist Fowle in Exeter, New Hampshire, who produced a small run of the text between 16 and 19 July 1776 for his newspaper, the New Hampshire Gazette or Exeter Morning Chronicle.These “Exeter Declarations” were printed quickly, on modest paper, for immediate distribution rather than long-term preservation. Over time, most copies were discarded, damaged or lost. Today, only 11 are known to survive, all held in US institutions until this discovery. The London copy is therefore unique not only for its rarity but for its location, offering a tangible link between the American Revolution and the British naval and governmental records that documented the conflict from the other side.How a Declaration ended up in British handsThe story of how this particular copy reached London begins with an American privateer named Dalton, a 20-gun brigantine commissioned by the Continental Congress to attack British shipping. In late 1776, the Dalton sailed from Newburyport, Massachusetts, with a mixed crew of about 120 men, including Americans, English, Irish, Scottish, French and Danish sailors, as well as at least one Black crew member, Daniel Cottle. During a stop on the Piscataqua River in New Hampshire, someone on board, most likely an officer, acquired a freshly printed Exeter Declaration.On Christmas Eve 1776, the Dalton was hunting for British prizes off the coast of Portugal when it encountered HMS Raisonable, a much larger 64-gun Royal Navy ship. After a seven-hour chase, the Dalton surrendered. Captain Fitzherbert recorded the capture in his log and took the American crew as prisoners. He then ordered one of his lieutenants to bring the Dalton, its senior officers and its papers into Plymouth for prize proceedings.Prize papers, procedure and a deliberate exceptionUnder British naval practice at the time, all papers found on a captured enemy ship had to be seized and presented to a prize court to determine whether the vessel and its cargo legally belonged to the enemy. The lieutenant acting as prize-captain swore that the only documents taken from the Dalton were its privateering commission and instructions from Congress. We now know that was not the full story.Captain Fitzherbert kept the Declaration for himself. He made copies of the Dalton’s commission and instructions and sent those to the Admiralty Secretary in Whitehall, along with a brief note mentioning signals and “another paper.” That “other paper” was the Exeter Declaration. By singling it out for immediate dispatch, Fitzherbert seems to have recognised its significance, even if Britain did not yet acknowledge the United States as a sovereign nation. From that point, the document remained within British government records, passing from the Admiralty to the Public Record Office and finally to The National Archives, where it lay unnoticed until 2026.The Dalton’s crew and their fateThe fate of the Dalton’s crew adds another layer to the story. After their capture, the sailors were imprisoned first on HMS Belleisle in Plymouth harbour and later at the Old Mill Prison, which by the end of 1779 held nearly 300 American prisoners. Among them was 19-year-old Charles Herbert of Newburyport, who kept a diary describing the harsh conditions and several escape attempts, including an elaborate tunnel dug beneath the prison.Herbert’s account reveals how the ideals of the Declaration played out in the lives of ordinary people. These men had volunteered to serve on a ship authorised by the Continental Congress, many of them attacking the shipping of their own nations of birth. Some were free Black sailors, others were immigrants or transient workers drawn into the conflict by opportunity, ideology or circumstance. Their experiences of capture, imprisonment and eventual release form a human counterpoint to the grand political claims of the document they carried.Conservation and scientific examinationOnce the Declaration was identified, collection care specialists at The National Archives undertook delicate conservation work. The document had been bound into a volume of Fitzherbert’s letters, attached with adhesive. Senior conservator Jillian Harrold used an ultrasonic humidifier to introduce moisture in a controlled way, softening the glue so the broadside could be gently separated with a spatula. A long tear across the middle was repaired using fine Japanese paper and wheat starch paste, stabilising the sheet for future handling and display.Heritage scientist Marc Vermeulen then examined the paper and printing. Raking light photography revealed the original fold lines, showing how the sheet had been handled and stored over time. Microscopic analysis detected blue fibres typical of rag paper made from recycled textiles, as well as yellowish plant fragments that may include hemp hurd. Transmitted light imaging showed the chain and laid lines characteristic of handmade paper, though no watermark was found. These features suggest a comparatively lower-quality paper, consistent with the urgent, economical printing conditions in wartime New England.What the discovery means for historiansFor historians of the American Revolution, the Exeter Declaration in London is more than a rare printing. It is a physical trace of how the ideas of independence travelled across the Atlantic, carried on a privateer ship, captured by the Royal Navy and filed within British government records as evidence in a prize case. The document’s presence in Admiralty papers underscores how intertwined British and American histories were during the war, even as the two sides fought to define their future relationship.The find also highlights the continuing importance of archival cataloguing and volunteer-led projects. The America 250 initiative, building on earlier work to catalogue Royal Navy captains’ letters from the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars, created the conditions for this discovery. Without systematic attention to these boxes of correspondence, the Declaration might have remained hidden for decades more.A new chapter in a 250-year storyThe Exeter Declaration will feature in The National Archives’ exhibition Revolution 250: America’s Independence Story 1763–1783, which runs from June to November 2026. Alongside three Dunlap Broadsides, the first official prints of the Declaration held in the UK, the newly found copy offers visitors a chance to see different early printings and consider how the text circulated in its first weeks.For Michael Scurr and the team behind the America 250 project, the discovery is a reminder that major historical documents can still surface in unexpected places. A volunteer opening a box of 18th-century naval letters in London has added a new chapter to the story of the Declaration of Independence, linking a small New Hampshire print shop, an American privateer captured off Portugal and the British naval bureaucracy that preserved, perhaps unintentionally, a unique piece of transatlantic history.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: BMC seeks agency to diversify funding, explore alternative finance for infrastructure projects
articles.summary: MUMBAI: BMC is looking to appoint a project implementing agency to help it develop a broader financing strategy and mobilise funds through alternative.
articles.body: MUMBAI: BMC is looking to appoint a project implementing agency to help it develop a broader financing strategy and mobilise funds through alternative sources for its growing infrastructure requirements, including water supply, wastewater, sanitation and urban infrastructure projects.The move comes as the BMC’s committed liabilities are are over Rs 2 lakh crores with major infrastructure projects like the Mumbai Coastal road -north, twin tunnels for Goregaon Mulund Link Road and the upgradation of sewage treatment plant underway.The civic body has invited e-tenders for an agency that will provide financial strategy, debt management and institutional coordination support, including identifying and structuring alternative financing options.According to the tender issued by the BMC’s Chief Accountant (Finance) on September 21, the selected agency will prepare a Capital Investment Plan (CIP) and a Debt Management Policy (DMP) and help the civic body mobilise funds through multiple financing instruments.The tender document states that BMC’s infrastructure requirements are growing in scale and complexity, creating a need to strengthen and diversify its financing capacity. The agency will be expected to identify projects that can attract financing, advise on financial structuring and help BMC access long-term capital on competitive terms.The proposed financing strategy will cover seven broad areas, including capital markets, climate and carbon finance, development finance, government support mechanisms, innovative and blended finance, and revenue enhancement measures.The agency will also advise BMC on municipal bonds, including green, sustainability, social and sustainability-linked bonds. Its mandate will include identifying opportunities for carbon credits, certification and monetisation, as well as helping the civic body access Central and state government grants, subsidies, low-interest loans and other schemes.BMC officials said it is separately in the process of appointing merchant bankers and other transaction intermediaries for specific assignments, including bond issuances. The proposed agency will therefore work alongside these intermediaries and provide end-to-end advisory, handholding, structuring and coordination support.An important part of the agency’s mandate will be to provide day-to-day support to BMC officials in their interactions with merchant bankers and other financial intermediaries, while also helping identify and structure additional sources of finance.“The agency will also assist the BMC Finance Department in preparing financial presentations, briefing notes and talking points for meetings with state government departments, external delegations, domestic and international study tours and apex bodies, including the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions,” states the tender document.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Pennsylvania's youth business fair grew from 60 booths in 2022 to 100 in 2026; kids ages 5 to 16 handled their own products, pricing and sales with no adults behind the tables
articles.summary: US News: Pennsylvania's youth business fair has grown from 60 booths in 2022 to 100 in 2026, turning a small community gathering into one of Central PA's most .
articles.body: Pennsylvania's youth business fair has grown from 60 booths in 2022 to 100 in 2026, turning a small community gathering into one of Central PA's most visible celebrations of kid-led enterprise. Children aged 5 to 16 run their own stalls, handling products, pricing, marketing and sales with no adults behind the tables, while parents and volunteers stay in the background as shoppers and supporters. The event, known as the Kidpreneurs Fair PA and hosted in Mechanicsburg, is part of the wider Acton Children's Business Fair network and is organised by local parents Ashruta Shettar and Pradeep Patil, who say the goal is to let kids learn entrepreneurship by doing rather than by watching, according to the fair's official site and the Children's Business Fair listing.A kitchen-table idea becomes a regional traditionThe Kidpreneurs Fair PA began around a family kitchen table in 2022. Ashruta Shettar and Pradeep Patil, IT professionals and small-business owners, were watching their twin daughters dream up products and realised that their children would learn more by actually selling something than by talking about business in the abstract. They set up the first fair with 60 young entrepreneurs, offering each child a simple booth, a table and a chance to test their ideas with real customers.From that first event, the fair quickly became a local tradition. In 2024, participation grew to more than 85 kidpreneurs, with families turning out in large numbers to support everything from handmade crafts to original recipes. By 2025, nearly 160 children filled the marketplace, and some participants began converting their fair-day experiments into ongoing micro-businesses that operated beyond the single event. The 2026 edition capped booths at 100 and added a special touch, with personalised letters from the Governor of Pennsylvania for every participant, signalling how far the fair had come in just a few years.The rule that makes it real: no adults behind the tableThe most distinctive feature of the fair is its core rule. Parents may help with the application and with transport, but on fair day, children must run their own booths. They set up their displays, greet customers, explain their products, handle money and make change. Adults are welcome as shoppers and cheerleaders, but they are not allowed to sell or promote a child's product. If a parent is found doing so, the child's business can be disqualified from the competition.This rule is designed to give children an authentic experience of entrepreneurship. It means that a 6-year-old selling friendship bracelets must decide how much to charge, how to arrange the table and how to talk to strangers about their work. A 14-year-old offering custom keychains or baked goods must think about costs, profit margins and how to stand out in a busy marketplace. The fair becomes a safe space to make mistakes, learn from them and try again next year with a better plan.How kids prepare their businessesThe application process itself is part of the learning. Children are asked to describe their product or service, set a price, estimate costs and explain how they will cover startup expenses. They must outline how they will advertise before the fair and how they will judge success at the end. Parents can assist with writing and calculations, but the expectation is that children do as much as possible on their own, appropriate to their age.Businesses are judged in six age categories, from 5 to 6 years old up to 15 to 16. Mixed-age groups are judged in the category of the oldest participant, and up to three children can share a single booth. The application fee is $35 per booth, fully refundable if the business is not accepted or if the family cancels at least a week before the event. Accepted applicants are notified on a rolling basis until the 100-booth cap is reached, creating a sense of urgency and planning for young founders.A marketplace of ideas and productsWalking through the fair feels like visiting a miniature version of a farmers market or craft fair, except every vendor is under 17. Booths feature handmade jewellery, slime and sensory toys, custom T-shirts, baked goods, art prints, pet treats, bath bombs and small services such as lawn care or tech help for neighbours. Some children build on hobbies, turning a love of drawing or baking into a branded product line. Others experiment with entirely new ideas, testing whether there is demand for a concept they have never tried before.Each business is given an 8-foot table, shared with one other vendor, under a tented outdoor setup at Messiah University's Eisenhower Campus Center in Mechanicsburg. Tablecloths are not provided, and electricity is not available, so children must design displays that work with simple materials. This constraint encourages creativity. A well-arranged table with clear pricing, attractive samples and a friendly pitch can make a big difference in how many customers stop and buy.Judges, awards and encouragementA panel of local business leaders, educators and community figures serves as judges for the fair. Past and current judges have included school heads, CEOs of regional organisations, commissioners from state advisory bodies, owners of small businesses and representatives from major employers such as The Hershey Company and IKEA. They evaluate each business on creativity, presentation and entrepreneurial spirit, offering feedback that is meant to encourage young founders long after the fair ends.While prizes and recognition matter, the organisers stress that the real reward is the experience. Children leave with a clearer sense of what it takes to run a business, from costing and pricing to customer service and marketing. Some go on to expand their fair-day ventures into regular income streams, selling online or at local markets. Others simply gain confidence, realising that they can create something, put it in front of strangers and handle the entire transaction themselves.Part of a larger movementThe Kidpreneurs Fair PA is part of the Acton Children's Business Fair network, which began in Austin, Texas, in 2007. That first event had just seven young entrepreneurs and about 25 attendees. Today, the Austin fair hosts more than 115 kidpreneurs and draws around 1,500 visitors, and similar fairs run in cities and towns across North America. The model is intentionally simple and replicable, relying on local hosts, volunteers and small sponsors to bring the experience to their own communities.In Pennsylvania, the fair is proudly sponsored by Sugaring NYC and supported by local donors and volunteers. The organisers say they believe principled entrepreneurs are heroes and role models for the next generation, whether they become famous business leaders or remain unsung owners of small neighbourhood enterprises. By giving children a structured, supportive environment to try entrepreneurship early, they hope to nurture a generation that sees business as a way to solve problems, serve others and build independence.Why this matters for families and schoolsFor parents and educators, the fair offers a practical complement to classroom learning. Children apply maths when they calculate costs and profits, use language arts when they write product descriptions and signage, and practise social skills when they interact with customers. They also learn resilience. Not every product sells out, not every display attracts a crowd, and not every idea works the first time. Those lessons, experienced in a low-stakes setting, can shape how children approach challenges in school and later in work.As the Kidpreneurs Fair PA continues to grow, its organisers face choices about how big to go, how to maintain quality and how to keep the focus on learning rather than competition. For now, the trajectory from 60 booths in 2022 to 100 in 2026 suggests strong demand from families who want their children to have this kind of hands-on experience. In a region known for its small businesses and community spirit, the fair has become a place where the next generation can practise being founders, one table at a time.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Decision unanimous': EC counters report of internal differences over SIR
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), saying all dec.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), saying all decisions related to the exercise were taken "unanimously".The poll body clarified that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling, but these did not amount to disagreement with the final decisions taken by the Commission.The clarification came after an Indian Express report triggered a row by claiming that the two Election Commissioners had raised objections to the Commission's decisions 14 times over the past 10 months during the SIR exercise.EC sources told PTI that all decisions taken by the Election Commission, including those related to the SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as well as Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Responding to queries, officials said Sandhu and Joshi had flagged issues related to the deletion of names from electoral rolls in various states and the handling of voter data.Officials also pointed out that the law governing the Election Commission, as well as a Supreme Court judgment, provides that decisions should, as far as possible, be taken unanimously. Where unanimity is not possible, the majority view prevails.Opposition slams CECMeanwhile, opposition sharpened its attack on the Election Commission over the SIR, claiming it was meant to target electors not aligned to the BJP and its allies.Urging the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognizance of the issue, several opposition parties attacked Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and accused him of becoming a puppet of those in power.In a social media post, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the poll panel of hatching a conspiracy to "wipe out democracy.""This is an extremely serious news that in the past 10 months, 2 Election Commissioners have registered their objections 14 times against the Election Commission's wrong decisions," Akhilesh said."This directly means that all Election Commissioners are not able to perform their rightful duties. If the members of an independent body do not have the freedom to carry out just actions or if there is no hearing of theirs, then these are extremely fatal and dangerous circumstances for democracy. For some people to betray democracy by becoming puppets of those in power is a grave constitutional crime. This is nothing less than a conspiracy to wipe out democracy," he added.Mamata Trinamool Congress (MTMC) also slammed CEC Kumar and said that the opposition should reintroduce the impeachment motion against Kumar in Parliament."Five months ago, more than 60 Rajya Sabha Members of Parliament... when only 50 were needed, wrote to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha moving a motion to remove the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, that was five months ago. Now today, after this big news break that two Election Commissioners objected to many of the CEC's actions, it's time to bring out the Rajya Sabha motion to impeach the CEC and save democracy," MTMC's Derek O' O'Brien said.The issue is likely to escalate further as leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been vehement in his criticism of the Election Commission and the SIR process, alleging that it has resulted in the denial of voting rights.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A 97-year-old Brisbane bowls club facing demolition is saved in a $6 million deal after Bowls Queensland rejected an offer $1 million higher to keep both greens
articles.summary: Rest of World News: For a club that spent years staring down the prospect of demolition, the future of Coorparoo Bowls Club now looks very different. The 97-year-old Bris.
articles.body: For a club that spent years staring down the prospect of demolition, the future of Coorparoo Bowls Club now looks very different. The 97-year-old Brisbane institution will remain a place for bowls and community gatherings after the site was sold for $6 million to a local investor, ending plans that could have replaced the club with high-rise apartments, states the latest news report by ABC News. The deal preserves both bowling greens and gives the historic club a chance to enter its next chapter without losing the character that has defined it for generations.A campaign that kept the greens aliveAs per the ABC News report, the sale follows a multi-year campaign by the Coorparoo Bowls Club committee, which had been fighting to protect the venue and was facing eviction in May this year. Rather than see the site disappear under a redevelopment, the club will now remain in place under new ownership. Bowls Queensland reached the $6 million agreement with Coorparoo local Will Griffin of Griffin Hospitality Group after considering competing offers. The organisation rejected an offer that was $1 million higher, prioritising an agreement that would keep bowls operating at the site.That decision means both existing greens will stay. One will be available for competitions, while the other will cater to casual players, preserving the club's role for both organised games and everyday community use.Plans for a renewed clubhouseThe new ownership is expected to bring changes to the venue, but not a complete transformation, adds the online report. Griffin Hospitality plans to renovate the clubhouse, bar and kitchen while retaining the atmosphere and character associated with the club. The aim is to make the venue more welcoming for bowlers, families and visitors while keeping the sport at its centre. The plans also position the club as more than a sporting venue, with space for meals, social gatherings and community activities alongside regular bowls. For a property that had been facing a very different future, the approach offers a way to modernise the venue without erasing its history.The committee stays onThe report also states that the committee that led the campaign to save Coorparoo Bowls Club will remain involved, signing a five-year lease to continue running the club. That arrangement keeps the people who have helped steer the club through its uncertain years connected to its future. With both greens protected, renovations planned and the existing committee remaining at the helm, Coorparoo Bowls Club has avoided demolition and secured a path forward. After nearly a century at the heart of the local community, the club will continue rolling bowls rather than making way for towers.Image Courtesy: ABC NewsCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: IIT-Bombay on boil: Professor sent on leave, student's parents 'driven' out of Mumbai; all you need to know
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The parents of IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode alleged they were driven out of Mumbai in a “private car” early Wednesday morning despite repea.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The parents of IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode alleged they were driven out of Mumbai in a “private car” early Wednesday morning despite repeatedly telling the driver that they intended to stay in the city and begin a hunger strike outside the Powai institute.The family, accompanied by their lawyer, said they reached the Karanja Lad area of Washim district by early morning. They had earlier spoken to the media outside the Crime Branch office in Bandra and later outside the IIT-Bombay campus in Powai.The development came as the Mumbai Crime Branch continued its investigation into Sahil's death and his parents demanded the immediate arrest of the two people named in the FIR.Family alleges they were taken in private carAccording to lawyer Nikhil Wakode, after the family left the IIT-Bombay gate in Powai, they were asked by men in plain clothes to shift to another vehicle.“We were asked to change the car by some people who were not in uniform. I was wondering why my clients were being taken in a private car when they had their own vehicle. So I too sat along with them. I don't know the name of the officers, they were in mufti,” Wakode said.Sahil's father, Ravindra Wakode, said the family repeatedly asked the driver where they were being taken.“He kept saying, ‘I am dropping you home’,” Wakode said, who added, they were also tired and sleepy.The family said they had made it clear that they did not want to return home and planned to begin a hunger strike outside IIT-Bombay from Wednesday morning.“I have taken permission for that,” Wakode said.Wakode claimed police vehicles initially followed the private car but were no longer visible after it entered the Samruddhi Expressway.“We then told the driver that we wanted to use the washroom and got off the vehicle,” he said.He said the family was returning to Mumbai and remained determined to begin the hunger strike outside IIT-Bombay.“I want justice for my son. Do you realise that 100 hours have passed and no action has been taken against the offenders?” he said.IIT-Bombay professor sent on leaveMeanwhile, IIT-Bombay professor Suryanarayana Doolla, who has been named as an accused in the case, has been sent on leave to facilitate an impartial probe.The institute on Monday removed Doolla as dean of Administrative Affairs following protests over Sahil's death.Doolla was sent on leave after being removed from the dean's post to enable an impartial investigation. No classes are currently underway, they added.The Mumbai Crime Branch is investigating Sahil's death.Parents demand arrest of two accusedRavindra Wakode on Tuesday demanded the immediate arrest of the two accused named in the FIR, saying the family wanted a fair investigation and justice for their son.“No action has been taken. If they have taken action, they should show us. Why haven't they arrested them? Where is the arrest? Have they arrested them?” Ravindra Wakode said.He said the family had given their statements to the authorities and would not interfere with the investigation. He also said they planned to hold a peaceful protest in Powai.“We held a press conference in Powai as well. And now, we are going to sit on a protest strike. We want to do this peacefully. We will not create any obstacles in their investigation,” he said.Ravindra Wakode also alleged that there had been previous incidents of student suicides and questioned whether those cases had been properly investigated.“Look at the background of the IIT student. My son's death was murder, and there have been suicides before this as well. Why hasn't this been investigated yet? You should see their FIR. Why are these cases always hushed up?” he said.He said the family was not concerned about any committee and wanted action against those named in the FIR.“We don't care about the committee. All we want is for our son to get justice. They should be arrested first. Arrest them, and then conduct your investigation. We have no problem with the investigation,” he added.Lawyer says family wants 'fair investigation'Sahil's family lawyer Nikhil Kambale said the family's demand was the arrest of the two accused named in the FIR — Shirish Kedare and Suryanarayan Dudhla — after which the investigation could proceed.“This is part of an investigation. It doesn't matter what we say, it won't affect the investigation. My client's only expectation and repeated demand is that the accused named in the FIR, both accused, should be arrested immediately,” Kambale said.Responding to claims made by the IIT-Bombay Faculty Forum, Kambale said the family did not want to get involved in allegations and counter-allegations.“These claims are irrelevant. Such claims will keep coming and going. We will respond to their claims, and they will respond to our reaction, but that won't solve anything. Our only point is that the investigation should be fair,” he said.Kambale said the family wanted the Crime Branch to conduct a fair probe and ensure justice for Sahil.“The crime branch is doing their job; we want them to arrest the accused and provide justice. My client just wants justice for his child. There is no intention to react; nothing will happen by reacting. The case will not grow. We want a fair investigation,” he said.ABVP seeks probe before actionThe Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) on Wednesday called for a thorough investigation into Sahil's death and said action should be taken against whoever is found responsible after the probe.ABVP national general secretary Virendra Singh Solanki said taking action without establishing the facts would not be appropriate.“Our workers are already involved in this. We have demanded an investigation. Taking any action without a detailed understanding of the matter and ascertaining the truth would not be appropriate. Therefore, we have demanded a complete investigation,” he said.“Once the investigation is completed, action should be taken against whoever is found responsible,” Solanki added.Sahil, a second-year BTech student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, was found hanging in his hostel room on September 18 evening, hours after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone to access AI platform during a mid-semester examination.His parents have alleged that he faced caste-based discrimination and demanded action against those they hold responsible for his death.Sahil's mother, Sonali Wakode, claimed that her son had told the family he was being tortured, abused and humiliated because of his caste.She claimed Sahil “specifically told us that Professor Suryanarayana Doolla would say, 'I am from an upper caste and you are from a lower caste' and this had been continuing for around three months.”She also questioned the institute's initial claim that Sahil had been caught using AI platform during an examination, saying anyone making allegations of cheating must provide evidence.Ravindra Wakode said the truth would emerge only after the accused in the case were arrested.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Psychology says children who tear up their own drawings or homework may be putting more pressure on themselves than parents realize
articles.summary: A child finishes a drawing, looks at it for a few seconds and suddenly tears the paper in half. Another rubs out an entire page of homework because on.
articles.body: A child finishes a drawing, looks at it for a few seconds and suddenly tears the paper in half. Another rubs out an entire page of homework because one answer is wrong. Some children may refuse to show their parents something they have made because, in their eyes, it is “not good enough”. To a parent, this can look like frustration over a small mistake. But sometimes, the reaction can be much bigger than the mistake itself.Research on childhood perfectionism suggests that some children can become unusually concerned about errors and judge their own work harshly when it does not match the standard they have in mind. That does not mean every child who tears up a drawing is a perfectionist. But repeated reactions of this kind can be worth noticing.When one small mistake ruins the whole thingImagine a child who has spent 30 minutes drawing a house. Everything looks fine except one window is slightly uneven. Instead of accepting it, the child tears the page. The parent may see a perfectly good drawing with one imperfect detail. The child may see only the mistake. Perfectionism is not simply wanting to do well. Researchers distinguish between setting high standards and becoming overly concerned with mistakes, self-criticism and the possibility of failure.A 2020 meta-analysis involving 21,272 participants found that the more self-critical side of perfectionism was associated with poorer academic outcomes and unhelpful behaviours such as academic stress and burnout. The researchers also distinguished perfectionism from a healthier pursuit of excellence.Some children can be much harder on themselvesA child does not always need a parent to point out a mistake. Sometimes the criticism comes from the child. They may erase an answer repeatedly because the handwriting is not neat enough. They may start a drawing again because one line went wrong. They may become upset when they cannot solve something immediately. Research involving 203 children aged 8 to 12 examined two different aspects of self-oriented perfectionism: striving for high standards and being highly critical of oneself. The study found that parental expectations were associated with the striving side, while parental criticism was associated with the more self-critical form. The self-critical form was also associated with more negative effects.A child's reaction to mistakes can become part of a patternOne torn worksheet is not enough to tell a parent anything. Children rip paper because they are angry, tired, frustrated or simply having a bad day. Younger children are also still learning to regulate strong emotions. The concern is when the same reaction appears repeatedly. A child may refuse to submit work unless it looks perfect, repeatedly erase or restart assignments, become very upset after small mistakes, avoid trying something difficult because they might get it wrong, compare their work with others and immediately dismiss their own or say things such as “I'm bad at this” after one mistake.Research has found links between perfectionistic concerns and difficulty coping with mistakes. A 2017 study of school-aged children found that parental criticism was associated with the self-critical form of perfectionism, while this form of perfectionism was associated with negative affect.What parents say after a mistake can matterThis does not mean parents cause perfectionism simply by expecting children to do well. Children can develop perfectionistic tendencies through several influences, including their own temperament, social experiences and the standards they place on themselves. But research suggests that the way children experience parental expectations and criticism can be relevant. A meta-analysis covering 46 studies and 13,364 participants examined the relationship between parenting behaviours and perfectionism. It found that parental expectations had positive relationships with several forms of perfectionism, while parental criticism was uniquely associated with socially prescribed perfectionism. The researchers also found evidence that parents' own perfectionistic tendencies can correspond with similar tendencies in their children.That makes the response to a mistake worth considering. If a child tears up a drawing and hears, “Why can't you do it properly?”, the mistake can become bigger. A response such as, “You didn't like that part? What would you like to change?” keeps the focus on the work rather than the child's ability.Don't rush to fix the drawingParents often want to rescue the child immediately.“It looks beautiful.” “Don't tear it.” “Let me fix that part.” But constant reassurance may not teach a child what to do with imperfection. Instead, parents can help children stay with a small mistake. “Which part are you unhappy with?” “Do you want to change it or leave it?” “What happens if we keep going?” These questions allow the child to make a choice without turning the mistake into a crisis.What parents can say insteadWhen a child tears up homework or a drawing, the first response does not have to be, “Why did you do that?” Try: “I can see that mistake really bothered you.” “Do you want to try again or take a break?” “What part would you like to change?” “It doesn't have to be perfect to be finished.” And sometimes, simply: “Making mistakes is part of learning.” A torn drawing may be nothing more than a child's moment of frustration. But if a child repeatedly destroys their work, refuses to try unless they know they can do it perfectly, or becomes extremely distressed by ordinary mistakes, it may be worth looking beyond the behaviour.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: A four-bedroom waterfront home was completed in California in 2026; within months, the Belvedere property is listed for $32 million; the newly built estate comes with sweeping bay views and luxury amenities
articles.summary: News News: Less than a year after completion, the newly built mansion at 46 Cliff Road in Belvedere hit the market. The waterfront mansion is asking $32 million,.
articles.body: Less than a year after completion, the newly built mansion at 46 Cliff Road in Belvedere hit the market. The waterfront mansion is asking $32 million, the San Francisco Business Times reported. The three-storey home sprawls across 5,000 square feet with four bedrooms, five bathrooms, and what may be its most prized perk: direct access from street to water, which is rare on Belvedere Island. The current owners, who acquired the property this year, are putting it back on the market as they are building a larger residence elsewhere.What the buyer getsIt is one of the very few places in the world where land, water, and land conspire to create something magnificent. Most homes on the island either face the water or back onto the street. This one does both. So the buyer really gets unobstructed views across the bay towards San Francisco and the Golden Gate Bridge!Set at the water's edge, this mansion has a magnificent view of the San Francisco skyline, the Golden Gate Bridge, the Marin Headlands, Sausalito, and Mount Tamalpais. The house comes with four bedrooms and five full bathrooms. The primary suite includes a walk-in wardrobe. The kitchen is clean and functional: stone counters, a gas cooktop, wine refrigerator, dishwasher, range hood, and the standard ensemble of appliances that make a modern kitchen feel complete. Wood and stone flooring flows through the main living areas, anchoring the open layout without the visual weight of wall-to-wall carpet.The living room opens onto a terrace where the bay views actually land. A fireplace and deck access make the space feel like somewhere people might actually spend time. There is a spa with a built-in hot tub outdoors and a grill, along with multiple terraces that appeal to buyers who are great hosts. The modern construction includes a two-car garage, contemporary amenities throughout, and the kind of finish that commands this price tag before the first occupant moves in.The lot itself carries history. It was last sold in May 2019 for $2.1 million before any development. The transformation from vacant land to turnkey luxury home in roughly seven years reflects the velocity of wealth appreciation in this enclave. Belvedere Island's geography, surrounded by water, with limited buildable land, creates scarcity, which keeps prices climbing.Tania Toubba, the agent listing the property through Sotheby's International Realty, told the outlet that the newly built home's owners intended to live there long-term, but they ultimately “decided they need more space and are currently building a larger home.” Quinta Properties LLC, a local family-owned builder linked to Rudolph Koppl, owns the property, the outlet reported.A market in motionThe $32 million listing arrives amid a flurry of activity on the peninsula. Last month, 125 Belvedere Avenue was sold for $16.9 million, sidestepping an auction through Concierge Auctions. Down the road, a nearly 10,000-square-foot property at 20 Crest Road is asking $50 million, which would set a residential record for Marin County if the sale closes at that figure.The market really started moving upwards after Apple design chief Jony Ive completed a surprise $73 million acquisition in September 2025. Ive bought four homes on the peninsula in a single off-market deal: three consecutive houses on Golden Gate Avenue and another on Beach Road. Ive's largest property, with five bedrooms, 11 bathrooms and four fireplaces, was sold for $43.5 million. This move assured Belvedere's ultra-luxury tier and appeared to catalyse price increases across the island almost immediately.Agents were flooded with calls after Ive's purchase became public. One estate down the hill from his compound bumped its asking price 10% within days. For a property in Belvedere, a 10% jump means adding millions without changing a brick.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Trump-Xi summit: $14 billion Taiwan arms deal hangs over Washington talks
articles.summary: US News: Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to press US President Donald Trump to halt arms sales to Taiwan when the two leaders meet in Washington this .
articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to press US President Donald Trump to halt arms sales to Taiwan when the two leaders meet in Washington this week. Sources have informed Reuters that Beijing is likely to invoke a 1982 US-China agreement that commits Washington to gradually reducing weapons sales to Taipei.The issue is likely to be among the most sensitive points in Xi’s talks with Trump, as Beijing considers Taiwan a core sovereignty issue and has repeatedly demanded an end to US arms sales to the self-governed island.Three sources briefed on US-China discussions told Reuters that Beijing is expected to raise its interpretation of the third of the three US-China joint communiques, signed in 1982.Under the communique, Washington said it intended to gradually reduce its arms sales to Taiwan and did not seek to maintain long-term weapons sales to Taipei.But an accompanying memo by then-US President Ronald Reagan said the US commitment to reduce arms sales was “conditioned absolutely” on China’s continued commitment to resolving differences with Taiwan peacefully.The distinction is significant because China has sharply expanded its military activity around Taiwan in recent years, including military exercises involving live missile tests. Chinese forces now operate around the island on an almost daily basis, according to Reuters.$14 billion Taiwan deal remains on holdThe Trump administration approved an $11 billion arms package for Taiwan in December, described as the largest such package to date. But a second package worth about $14 billion has remained on hold for months.Trump said after meeting Xi in Beijing in May that he was keeping the package in abeyance and described it as a “very good negotiating chip”.A White House official said Trump would decide on the new package within a relatively short period.Trump approved more arms sales to Taiwan during his first term than any previous US president, the official said, adding that his second-term approvals in the first year had already exceeded the total approved during all four years of Joe Biden’s presidency.Taiwan’s foreign ministry said it was closely monitoring the US-China exchanges while maintaining communication with Washington.Beijing wants arms deliveries stopped China is also seeking an end to deliveries of weapons that Taiwan has already ordered from the US, according to the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the discussions.One source said Xi could tell Trump that Taiwan was the “provocateur” and the source of instability in US-China relations, while accusing Taipei of changing the status quo.Beijing could offer cooperation in putting pressure on Iran over the Middle East war in return, the sources said.China’s foreign ministry has said Washington must honour the three joint communiques and previous commitments on Taiwan, calling this a necessary condition for stable and healthy US-China ties.The US, however, maintains a “one China” policy under which it does not take a formal position on Taiwan’s sovereignty and acknowledges, without endorsing, Beijing’s position that Taiwan is part of China.Washington is also required by US law to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, despite the absence of formal diplomatic relations between the US and Taipei.Xi could ‘lecture’ Trump on TaiwanThe 1982 agreement is not the only document shaping the US position on Taiwan.The “Six Assurances” issued to Taiwan that year, but declassified only in 2020, stated that Washington had not agreed to set a date for ending arms sales to Taiwan or to consult Beijing before approving such sales.US lawmakers have also urged Trump not to weaken Washington’s support for Taipei ahead of his meeting with Xi.Republican senator Pete Ricketts, who chairs the Senate foreign relations subcommittee on East Asia, said last week that Trump should make clear that US policy on Taiwan had not changed.John Moolenaar, the Republican chairman of the House Select Committee on China, separately told Trump that Chinese objections to US arms sales and security cooperation with Taiwan and other Asian allies should be rejected.Matt Pottinger, who served as deputy national security adviser during Trump’s first administration, said he did not expect a substantive change on Taiwan during the summit.But he predicted Xi would likely “lecture” Trump at length on Taiwan, as he had done in previous meetings with US presidents.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
